title: Salade Nicoise
subtitle: The Provencal composed salad
excerpt: Tuna, green beans, boiled eggs, olives, anchovies, and tomatoes arranged over lettuce with a sharp mustard vinaigrette. The classic version of this Provencal salad uses no cooked potatoes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Salade nicoise is a signature dish of Nice and the Cote d'Azur. The traditional version, as defined by Nicois purists including Jacques Medecin, mayor of Nice and cookery writer, contains no cooked ingredients other than the eggs and green beans.

recipeTools.notes: For blanching the green beans and boiling the eggs.

content.text: Salade nicoise is a composed salad of tuna, green beans, hard-boiled eggs, tomatoes, black olives, and anchovies on a bed of lettuce, dressed in a sharp vinaigrette. Everything is arranged separately, not tossed together. The best versions use good tinned tuna, ripe tomatoes, and the strongest black olives you can find.

Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, then drain and transfer to cold water. Peel and halve when cool. Blanch the green beans in boiling salted water for 3 minutes until just tender but still bright green. Drain and refresh in cold water.
Make the dressing by whisking the mustard with the red wine vinegar and a pinch of salt, then slowly whisk in the olive oil until emulsified. Season with pepper.

Arrange the lettuce leaves over a large platter or four plates. Dress lightly with some of the vinaigrette. Arrange the green beans, tomatoes, tuna (broken into chunks), eggs, olives, anchovies, and red onion separately over the lettuce.
Drizzle the remaining vinaigrette over everything and serve immediately.
